avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin-potentiating supplements (Ginkgo biloba, Garlic, Ginger)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ceftriaxone may displace warfarin from protein binding and reduce vitamin K synthesis via microbiome disruption; combined with anticoagulant supplements increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor INR closely if coadministration necessary; counsel patient on bleeding signs

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium/Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Divalent cations can chelate ceftriaxone in GI tract, reducing antibiotic absorption and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; take ceftriaxone first, then supplements

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics (Lactobacillus, Saccharomyces)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ceftriaxone disrupts normal microbiota; probiotics may help restore intestinal flora but timing affects efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Administer probiotics at least 2-3 hours apart from ceftriaxone; continue during and after therapy

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin K supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ceftriaxone may reduce vitamin K synthesis via microbiome disruption; supplementation may partially mitigate coagulopathy risk
caution_supplements.action: Consider vitamin K supplementation if prolonged therapy; monitor PT/INR if at risk

avoid_foods.name: High-calcium dairy products (taken simultaneously)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium chelates cephalosporin, reducing bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Separate dairy intake by 2+ hours from ceftriaxone administration

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Cephalosporins rarely cause disulfiram-like reaction; alcohol may worsen GI side effects like nausea and diarrhea
caution_foods.action: Limit alcohol consumption during therapy; monitor for increased GI upset

caution_foods.name: Fermented foods (sauerkraut, kimchi, yogurt)
caution_foods.mechanism: High histamine content may be poorly tolerated if ceftriaxone-induced dysbiosis impairs histamine metabolism
caution_foods.action: Monitor for histamine intolerance symptoms (flushing, headache); reduce intake if symptomatic

monitoring_notes: Ceftriaxone undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism, reducing CYP interactions; however, microbiome disruption poses risks for vitamin K deficiency, secondary infections (C. difficile), and altered drug metabolism of other agents. Monitor PT/INR in at-risk patients, assess for diarrhea/CDI, and educate on chelation interactions with divalent cations and concurrent supplements.
